1.explanation:
1. We import the FileUploaderDropContainer component directly from its source path.  
2. We use @testing-library/react to render the component into a container.  
3. We leverage jest-axe (which wraps axe-core) to scan that container for accessibility violations.  
4. Because FileUploaderDropContainer nests an <input> inside a role="button" container, axe-core v4.2.0+ will report a 'nested-interactive' violation.  
5. Running this test with axe-core pinned to v4.2.0 or later reproduces the failing output shown in your bug‐report screenshots.  

To reproduce, add this test file under your __tests__ folder, ensure your package.json specifies "axe-core": "^4.2.0", install jest-axe, then run `yarn jest FileUploaderDropContainerA11y.test.js`. The test will fail with the nested-interactive error described.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering the FileUploaderDropContainer, the outer element is a <label> with role="button" (or a <div> with role="button") and it contains an <input type="file"> inside. Starting with axe-core v4.2.0, axe flags this as a "nested-interactive" violation because there is an interactive element (the file input) nested inside another element given a button role. Screen‐readers will not announce the inner control properly when an interactive control is its descendant.
